scope: Proposition 9.6 (The discovered mean) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 96. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let τ be one of the fixed stopped sweeps above, with limiting explored set Aτ , and write Mτ = E[h | Eτ ] as a distribution on tests. On each connected compact localization Q ⊂ int Q+ above at positive distance from W0 and the moving seed, Mτ is the finite signed sum Mτ = b0 + 2a X j visible in the localized list ϵj1O(Ccan j ). (9.8) Here b0 = 0 for the original free family. For the wired composite exploration, b0 ∈ {−a, a} is the label of the initial pointed wired hole containing the region. The sum is finite on each such localization because its contributor list is finite. An invisible entry has zero contribution. Consequently Mτ is a constant distribution on every ball missing W0, the moving seed, and the canonical supports associated with its local contributors.
